subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a parent-self-only tool denial policy for delegated sessions, and what public syntax and deny-wins semantics should define that boundary?
rationale: The missing source behavior is clear, but adding it changes the command/file-tool authority boundary between requester and child sessions, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Design explicit delegate-only policy
options.body: Adopt a first-class `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly` policy with ordinary `deny` remaining absolute, plus audit diagnostics, docs, and native/ACP/Gateway coverage before implementation.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance
options.body: Keep the current rule that child sessions cannot regain tools removed from the requester, accepting separate agent profiles or prompt guidance as the supported pattern.

options.title: Fold into delegated permissions
options.body: Defer this into a unified spawned-session permission model so parent-self-only delegation and per-spawn child narrowing share one API.

recommendation.title: Design explicit delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a first-class `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly` policy with ordinary `deny` remaining absolute, plus audit diagnostics, docs, and native/ACP/Gateway coverage before implementation.
